question: After breaking below our prior $401.77 stop to $399.05, does Intuitive sit in a Stage 4 breakdown or a Stage 1 base—and can any realistic support band clear 1.50:1 asymmetry?

epigraph.quote: When a stock breaks its 30-week moving average and prior structural stop on rising volume, you respect the Stage 4 gate before guessing where the bottom sits.
epigraph.author: Weinstein Tape Discipline

web_blocks.title: 8.1 Stage 4 vs. Stage 1 Ledger Reconciliation & Prior Stop Breach

web_blocks.html: On November 20, 2026, ISRG closed at $399.05 (-2.01% daily, -10.04% weekly, -10.09% monthly, -29.54% YTD), dropping straight through our prior $401.77 structural stop [22, 23]. Our two automated technical feeds diverge and require transparent reconciliation. The primary market-facts ledger (facts_US_2026-11-20.json) tags ISRG as Stage 1 (Basing) because the 50-day SMA ($423.51) still slopes higher than 21 days ago ($395.04) and 63-day relative strength reads +16.47% [23]. However, our TradingView snapshot (snapshots_US_2026-11-20.json) classifies ISRG as STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED, AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN) [23].

We enforce the stricter STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) classification because price action broke every key weekly and daily floor [23]. At $399.05, shares sit -1.77% below the 30-week SMA ($406.23), -5.00% below the 10-week EMA ($420.05), -5.78% below the 50-day SMA ($423.51), and -6.70% below a declining 200-day SMA ($427.69, down from $472.32 sixty-three sessions ago) [22, 23]. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 sits in a Downtrend (10 distribution days. only 38.8% of stocks above 50-DMA), and ISRG itself logged 7 distribution days in 25 sessions [23].

book_subsections.title: Why the $401.77 Breach Settled the Technical Debate
paragraphs: Technical analysis earns its keep when it prevents you from rationalizing a falling knife inside a great company. One week ago, Intuitive Surgical hovered at $443.59 inside a tight squeeze, and our prior framework set a hard structural stop at $401.77. Over the next five sessions, shares dropped 10.04 percent, closing on November 20, 2026 at $399.05—slicing cleanly beneath $401.77 on 1.07 times 30-day average volume.

Notice the informative split between our two automated feeds. The market-facts ledger still tags ISRG as Stage 1 Basing because the 50-day SMA at $423.51 sits higher than it did 21 trading days ago and 63-day relative strength holds +16.47 percent. Yet our TradingView evaluation classifies ISRG as Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED, AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN). Look at the moving-average stack and you see why Stage 4 governs: $399.05 sits below the 30-week SMA ($406.23), 10-week EMA ($420.05), 50-day SMA ($423.51), and a falling 200-day SMA ($427.69, down from $472.32 three months ago). Across the broader market, the S&P 500 is in a Downtrend with 10 distribution days and only 38.8 percent of stocks above their 50-day averages.

book_subsections.title: Testing Realistic Stage-4 Support Against a True ATR Stop
paragraphs: Could a patient buyer still set a bid lower down and wait for support? Let us test the geometry honestly. Intuitive's 14-day Average True Range is $14.43, or 3.62 percent of the share price. Any real structural stop must sit at least 1.0x ATR—$14.43—below your entry band, or normal daily noise will shake you out immediately. That rules out the automated snapshot's $388.53 to $400.37 band with its $387.24 stop, which leaves barely $1.29 to $13.13 of room.

Instead, look at realistic Stage 4 support. Just below current price sits Pivot S1 at $394.45 and the 20-day swing low at $397.78; placing a 1.0x ATR stop beneath that shelf puts invalidation near $380.00—above our $375.00 SBC-adjusted Base Fair Value. Drop one shelf lower to Pivot S2 ($356.90) and the 63-day base low ($345.25), backed by a structural stop at $325.00 just under the $328.57 52-week low. Against $356.90, your risk is $31.90 per share (2.21x ATR), while upside to our $375.00 Base Fair Value is just $18.10—a 0.57-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio, far short of our 1.50-to-1 hurdle. Even at $345.25, payoff is only 1.47-to-1. When even realistic Stage 4 support fails 1.50-to-1 math, waiting for support becomes a hedge—and REJECTED is the only honest call.

book_subsections.title: Options Overlay and Institutional Flow Signals
paragraphs: Volume, sponsorship, and options data reinforce that patient stance. Institutional ownership ticked down 3.72 percent sequentially to 88.97 percent, while seven distribution days over the last 25 sessions show supply continues to meet rallies. Meanwhile, our options desk evaluated call-spread convexity and returned NO_OPTIONS_EDGE: no clean bullish call-spread strikes exist above $370 on the February 19, 2027 expiration inside a Stage 4 downtrend. Although 4-hour RSI at 27.06 may spark a brief oversold bounce toward the broken 30-week SMA ($406.23), we never buy oversold reflex rallies in Stage 4—we wait for a genuine multi-month Stage 1 base and Stage 2 breakout alongside an attractive ex-SBC price.

Turning to technical structure and multi-timeframe tape evidence as of November 20, 2026, Intuitive Surgical illustrates why fundamental admiration never overrides Stage 4 market structure. At $399.05, shares finished down 29.54% year-to-date and sliced right through our previously locked $401.77 structural stop, confirming supply distribution across daily and weekly charts.

Let us be completely transparent about why our two technical feeds show different stage numbers while pointing to the exact same caution. The daily-bar facts ledger tags ISRG as Stage 1 basing because shares sit near their 63-day low with flat short-term slope, whereas the weekly TradingView evaluation classifies ISRG as Stage 4 with a CAP_REJECTED timing gate because price sits well below declining moving averages and broader S&P 500 breadth has deteriorated into a 10-distribution-day Downtrend at 38.8% above 50-DMA.

Under strict Weinstein discipline and our no-FOMO options overlay, both equity and call options carry a hard NO_TRADE posture. Buying LEAPS calls into a Stage 4 breakdown against 48x trailing earnings while consolidated portfolio cash sits at just $2,540.35—only 3.38% of $75,110.60 total net worth—compounds drawdown risk unnecessarily.
